scope: Four requested frozen Appendix D statements only; no new experiment, source, rate, or canonical mutation.

inputs.prior: T21/report.json and T21/correction.tex; retain T21 lowest-weight correction; T23 does not re-audit T21

source.title: Nuclear Isomers: A Primer, Jain et al. (2021), Chapter 3

locators.content: odd-rank single-particle operators are quasispin scalar; same-seniority matrix elements independent of n
single-j parity and electric/magnetic seniority selection rules
same-seniority magnetic multipole matrix element reduced to n=v

findings.claim: All finite electromagnetic same-v decay exits at half filling require seniority change or shell mixing.
findings.conditions: For identical fermions in one j shell, odd-rank one-body operators are quasispin scalars and have n-independent same-v reduced matrix elements. M3 requires nonzero one-body RME, angular and parity selection, and energetic availability; M1 within one j is proportional to total J and has no off-diagonal transitions between distinct eigenstates. No physical nucleus or rate is asserted.

counterexample.energy: assume Ji state above Jf state; selection rules do not establish energy ordering

findings.validation: Racah factorial formula and independently constructed antisymmetric Fock states; exact 6j squared and Fock numerical agreement; even-rank E2 control vanishes at n=6.

findings.claim: det(-A)>0 is necessary and sufficient for existence of a finite nonnegative steady state for a particular source.
findings.conditions: det>0 iff for every fixed nonnegative source there is a unique nonnegative steady state globally attracting from arbitrary initial populations; equivalent to a loss channel reachable from each state. For det=0, a compatible special source may have a nonunique finite nonnegative steady state. For nonzero M=-A, compatibility is adj(M)S=0 for nonnegative source; if M=0 it is S=0.
findings.validation: Exact rational substitution; directly inspect positivity, nullspace, and column range.

findings.claim: The listed a=b=0, D1=D2 example is a valid degeneracy but incomplete; the claim that Jordan blocks guarantee boundedness is false.
findings.conditions: For nonnegative rates Delta=0 iff ab=0 and a-b+D1-D2=0. A nontrivial Jordan block can occur with one directed edge, and t exp(-gamma t) is required; for passive nonnegative source-free populations boundedness follows from nonincreasing total population, not Jordan form. All eigenvalues real and <=0.
findings.validation: Exact nilpotent square and exponential; numerical trajectories plus total derivative.

findings.claim: Closed and equal-loss fraction relaxation and first-order fast/slow roots.
findings.conditions: a+b>0; for equal-loss fraction, no source and nonzero total; for asymptotic roots, D_i/(a+b) small. Slow coefficient = (bD1+aD2)/(a+b), fast correction = (aD1+bD2)/(a+b); eigenmode ratio b/a only literal when a>0, with fractional form suitable for one-way limits.
findings.validation: Exact rational coefficient checks for two-way and one-way examples; fraction derivative independently checked.

findings.claim: A long-lived thermal bath and Born-Markov/secular approximations are necessary for a Lindblad equation.
findings.conditions: A nonthermal environment does not itself require Lindblad dynamics. Born-Markov and secular approximations are a common conditional microscopic derivation route, not necessary mathematical conditions for the GKSL form. No open-systems review is attempted.

validation.independence: Stdlib factorial Wigner formulas and newly constructed CG/Fock operators; no use of preexisting Fock control script or hardcoded M3 value as assertion.

limitations: Finite Fock calculations use floating arithmetic, with exact rational squared 6j; no experimentally observed decay, lifetime, or inferred ordering.
No external search needed; requested locally archived original consulted.
Only named passages were examined; no assurance about other appendices.
